reasoning: 1. TARGET ENGAGEMENT: Strong evidence of target engagement - lovastatin significantly reduced cholesterol (-27.25 mg/dL vs -3.77 mg/dL placebo) and LDL (-25.28 mg/dL vs -0.4 mg/dL placebo), confirming HMG-CoA reductase inhibition. 2. PATHWAY MODULATION: Mixed evidence of downstream biology changes. Some biomarkers showed directional changes (e-cadherin +0.67% vs -7.37% placebo, n-cadherin +5.91% vs -9.17% placebo, VEGF +4.81% vs -0.63% placebo) suggesting cellular pathway modulation, but changes were modest and no statistical significance reported. 3. CLINICAL TRANSLATION: Primary endpoint of histopathologic regression showed minimal effect. Pathologist 1 scored lovastatin 0.50 vs placebo -0.12, Pathologist 2 scored lovastatin 0.17 vs placebo 0.04. Clinical regression endpoint was essentially flat (4.03 vs 3.98, p=0.61). 4. POPULATION EFFECTS: Nevus count analysis showed potential subgroup signal - fewer patients had increased nevi on lovastatin (1 vs 7 on placebo), but overall effect was minimal. 5. CONFOUNDERS: No major trial design issues identified. 24-week duration appears appropriate for this endpoint. Sample size of 80 may have been underpowered for detecting small histologic changes.

failure_modes.evidence: Target was clearly engaged (cholesterol/LDL reduction) and some downstream biomarkers showed directional changes (e-cadherin, n-cadherin, VEGF), but the primary histopathologic regression endpoint showed minimal improvement and clinical regression was flat (p=0.61)
